title: onboarding a new external project also writes its private design.md, seeded from the captain's confirmed answers, so the first dispatch no longer fails with 'missing approved source …/design.md'; an existing design.md is never overwritten
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 the first external dispatch for maker-founder (BenjaminLu/agent-wardrobe) failed to pin with `missing approved source: ~/.firstmate/projects/maker-founder/design.md`. `fm-project.sh add` had written CONVENTIONS.md, state/config.yaml and the onboarding records, but no design.md, and firstmate hand-wrote the file before the round could start.

Mechanism (root cause). `bin/fm-project.sh add` execs `bin/fm-onboard.sh` (fm-project.sh:34-36), which runs `bin/lib/fm_onboard.py main`; on confirmed answers it calls `approve(home, e, p, answers)` (fm_onboard.py:427). `approve()` (fm_onboard.py:249-283) writes `state/onboarding/inspection.json`, `state/config.yaml` and `CONVENTIONS.md` (:280-282) and nothing else. The external design source is `FM_HOME/projects/<name>/design.md`: `fm_registry.py:509` resolves the `design` field of an external entry to `<home>/design.md` (`fm_project_get <name> design` prints it; fm-config.sh:983 exports it as FM_DESIGN), and `fm_autopilot.py:292-293` uses the same path. The pin reads it in `SpecPins.snapshot` (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:146-172): for an external project a missing file raises `missing approved source` (:163) because `collect()` (:174-180) does not pass `optional` for design.

Change. In `approve()` in bin/lib/fm_onboard.py, right after `atomic(home/'CONVENTIONS.md', render(p))` (:282), write `home/'design.md'` with the existing `atomic()` helper (fm_onboard.py:25-37: parent created 0700, file created 0600, refuses a symlink) when, and only when, no file exists at that path. If `home/'design.md'` is a symlink (dangling or not), raise ValueError('refusing symlink: …') like `atomic()` does; if it exists as a regular file, leave it byte-for-byte unchanged (re-onboarding and every other approve() caller keep firstmate's edits). Add one helper `design_seed(name, p, contract)` that returns the text, so tests can compare exactly. `name` is `home.name` (the project directory name, the same name the registry entry uses); `contract` is `answers['contract']` (already validated to carry `check`). No other function in fm_onboard.py changes; `edit()` and `drift()` never touch design.md.

Template (exact; `{x}` is the value, lists joined with ', ', booleans as Python `str()`): line 1 `# {name}: private design`; blank; `Written by fm project add at {p[confirmed_at]}. It is the approved design source every pin and round of this project reads. Firstmate edits it in place; onboarding never rewrites it.`; blank; `## 1. Product intent`; blank; `{p[product]}`; blank; `Captain intent ({p[confirmed_at]}): {p[captain]} — {p[intent]}`; blank; `## 2. Repository and checks`; blank; `- Repository: {p[repository]}, base {p[base]}`; `- Check: {contract[check]}`; `- Setup: {contract[setup]}` (this line only when the contract has a non-empty `setup`); `- Required checks: {required_checks joined}`; blank; `## 3. Policy`; blank; `- Land: {p[land]}; review: {p[review]}; post: {p[post]}`; `- Merge method: {p[merge_method]}; delete branch: {p[delete_branch]}`; blank; `## 4. Task intents`; blank; `Firstmate adds one subsection per task before its spec is pinned.`; the file ends with one newline. All values come from the validated policy `p` returned by `validate(p)` inside approve() and from the answers' contract; nothing from the engine registry and nothing from the target tree.

Pin acceptance (no code change). `SpecPins.snapshot` (fm_spec_pins.py:155-163) accepts any regular file at the external design path (`path.is_file()`, source 'local'), so the seeded file satisfies the pin with no change to bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py, fm-config.sh or fm_registry.py. `fm_project_paths.py:40` already refuses a symlinked `design.md` before any caller writes; keep that.

Test (fail-first; workers do not run suites; CI and the gates verify). (a) tests/onboard-cli.test.sh, after the existing successful `add ... --answers` (the `seed` project, line ~20): assert `$FM_HOME/projects/seed/design.md` exists; contains `# seed: private design`, `Private product brief`, `- Check: npm test`, `- Setup: npm ci`, `- Repository: owner/product, base main` and `## 4. Task intents`; has mode 600 (read with `python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(oct(os.stat(sys.argv[1]).st_mode&0o777))'`, expect `0o600`, so the check is the same on macOS and Linux); and `bash -c '. "$1/bin/fm-config.sh"; fm_project_get seed design "$2/config.yaml"' _ "$ROOT" "$eng"` (the file's existing idiom, tests/onboard-cli.test.sh:26) prints exactly that path. Before the answers run, the existing unconfirmed-proposal assertion gains `test ! -e $FM_HOME/projects/seed/design.md`. (b) tests/onboarding.test.sh `test_confirmation_write_edit_drift` (around :88-105): after the first `approve(home, ...)`, assert `(home/'design.md').read_text() == design_seed(home.name, p, self.answers()['contract'])`; then write `captain edit\n` to it, call `approve(home, self.e, self.p, self.answers())` again and assert the file still reads `captain edit\n`. (c) Same file: a case where `home/'design.md'` is a symlink to a temp file before approve() asserts ValueError and that the symlink target is unchanged. (a)-(c) fail on base (no design.md is written; `design_seed` does not exist).

Callers, mirrors and fixtures checked: `grep -rn 'approve(' bin tests` lists bin/lib/fm_onboard.py:427 (the add path), bin/fm-canary.sh:673 (external destroy fixture), tests/onboarding.test.sh:79, :81, :86, :91, :109, :110, :125, :146 and :159, tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh:25, tests/conventions-watch.test.sh:35, tests/conventions-publication.test.sh:77, tests/project.test.sh:216, tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh:21, tests/external-review-entrypoint.test.sh:26, tests/external-reviews.test.sh:261, tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py:593, tests/lib/external_entrypoints.py:74 (its `policy()` calls approve() again with other `delete` values: the first call creates design.md and later calls leave it alone; nothing there reads design.md) and tests/lib/external_stock.py:81 (approve) with :88 (it then writes its own `design.md` sentinel with `write_text`, which still overwrites as before). Each passes a temp home; the new file appears there and nothing asserts its absence or the `missing approved source` text. No caller writes design.md before approve() expecting it to be replaced. tests/dispatch.test.sh:86 defines an unrelated shell `approve`. None needs a change; the PR says so for each. tests/onboarding.test.sh's import line (:24) gains `design_seed`. Two suites reach approve() through `fm-project.sh add` rather than a direct call: tests/onboard-register.test.sh via `add_seed` (:34-35, called at :45, :56, :70, :80, :97, :105, :113, :156; it re-onboards the same home, so it relies on the 'existing design.md is left alone' rule) and tests/onboard-remote.test.sh:36 (one successful add; the refusals at :43 and :47 stop before approve(), fm_onboard.py:420-426). Neither asserts the home's contents, so neither changes. bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:13 imports from fm_onboard but not approve() and is unaffected.

Design (edit in place, no new section at the end, T-189). design/design.md §15.2, subsection '#### T-139 private onboarding contract': after the sentence ending `with explicit captain-confirmed checks, policy, product intent and commands.` (design.md:4870) add: `The same confirmation writes an initial private design.md beside it (T-226), seeded from the confirmed product intent, captain intent, check, setup, required checks and policy, with an empty task-intents section; it is the project's approved design source for every pin, and onboarding never overwrites an existing one.`

Out of scope: the content firstmate later writes into design.md, `fm project edit`/`drift`, the self project (`repo: .`, design/design.md), the pin code, the registry and CONVENTIONS.md rendering. Do not touch ~/.firstmate or any real FM_HOME.
